key_insight: Fight World Model separates combat rules from video generation: an executable engine decides what happens, while a rendering system visualizes it. This makes rule-consistent gameplay—not just plausible-looking combat—the foundation of the world model.
problem_solved: Video world models can produce convincing fights but struggle to maintain persistent game state and keep hit reactions and health updates consistent with executable rules.
method: Use an executable engine to maintain game state and resolve combat interactions.
Encode resolved outcomes with a deterministic compiler, using visual interaction proxies to connect combat execution with rendering.
Separate gameplay logic from visual generation to support programmable rules and extensible mechanics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a design pattern for combining explicit simulation logic with generative visuals. It targets customizable interactive worlds where gameplay consistency matters as much as visual realism.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: player input → combat engine → deterministic compiler → visual rendering.

paper_title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
paper_authors: Jiahua Li, Zixu John, Tom Zhong, Fuping Wu, Tianhao Xu
